propositions: Blocking links between two children of the same parent should record the exact pair with no promotion, not escalate to their common ancestor.
Type-tier comparability causes cross-subtree dependencies to escalate incorrectly to chain roots rather than nearest common ancestor children.
The redundancy check must evaluate the RESOLVED pair post-promotion, not the original pair, to catch ancestor-descendant relationships that emerge after escalation.
Non-blocking relations (relates_to, supersedes, discovered_from) must preserve original-pair redundancy checking and gain no new rejections from the blocking-pair widening.
The ancestor walk must terminate on parent cycles and walk to the root without a max_hops cap to correctly resolve deep hierarchies.
